description: Generic, CHEMISTRY-level (not enzyme-level) selectors that resolve a reaction-coordinate atom role onto a candidate's real atoms. Ligand roles are SMARTS matched with RDKit against a participant's modeling SMILES; the FIRST atom of the SMARTS is the reactive atom. Cofactor roles map to standard PDB CCD atom names.
scope_note: A selector is enzyme-agnostic but chemistry-specific. 'phosphate_activated_acyl_carbon' applies to ANY enzyme performing aminolysis of an acyl-phosphate or acyl-adenylate -- characterised or not, annotated or not -- but it does NOT apply to a thioester or a plain amide. This file is therefore a GROWING VOCABULARY, not a general solver: a new activation chemistry needs a new entry, keyed on the chemistry. Coverage today is carboxylate/amine functional groups, phosphate-activated acyl transfer, and nucleoside-triphosphate cofactors. Other cofactors (SAM, NAD, PLP, FAD, CoA) have no entries yet.
ambiguity_rule: A selector MUST resolve to one reaction site. The resolver fails closed on multiple matches that are chemically DISTINCT, because picking one arbitrarily scores a different reaction than the one being modelled -- e.g. 'amide_carbonyl_carbon' matches twice on a pantetheine-containing substrate, and the deprecated 'acyl_carbonyl_carbon' matches the reactive acyl carbon AND a distal carbonyl on an acyl-adenylate. Multiple matches are ACCEPTED only when every matched atom falls in one topological symmetry class (symmetry_equivalent), since homotopic sites are the same reaction: a symmetric bifunctional monomer has two interchangeable centres, while an unsymmetrically substituted one does not and is still refused.

changelog.v2: Added leaving-group and transition-state charge-centre selectors so near-attack geometry is fully specified for addition-elimination steps. Renamed the activated-acyl selectors to name the activating atom explicitly. Deprecated acyl_carbonyl_carbon as ambiguous.

ligand_smarts_notes.carboxylate_oxygen: General. Any enzyme acting on a carboxylate.
ligand_smarts_notes.amine_nitrogen: General. Primary/secondary amine, excluding amide N and imines.
ligand_smarts_notes.phosphate_activated_acyl_carbon: Electrophile of aminolysis/hydrolysis on an acyl-phosphate or acyl-adenylate. The ester oxygen to phosphorus is what makes this carbon electrophilic and is what distinguishes it from any other carboxyl on the same molecule. Verified unambiguous on both acyl-adenylate and acyl-phosphate intermediates.
ligand_smarts_notes.phosphate_activated_acyl_carbonyl_oxygen: Terminal carbonyl oxygen of that acyl group: the atom accumulating negative charge in the tetrahedral intermediate, i.e. the oxyanion-hole target.
ligand_smarts_notes.phosphate_activated_acyl_leaving_oxygen: Bridging ester oxygen joining the acyl carbon to the activating phosphorus; departs with AMP or phosphate.
ligand_smarts_notes.thioester_acyl_carbon: Vocabulary entry for thioester (CoA/ACP) acyl transfer. Validated unambiguous on a pantetheine thioester. NOT YET referenced by any reaction coordinate.
ligand_smarts_notes.amide_carbonyl_carbon: Vocabulary entry for amide hydrolysis. CAUTION: ambiguous on any substrate containing more than one amide; such a system needs a tighter, substrate-aware SMARTS. NOT YET referenced by any reaction coordinate.
ligand_smarts_notes.acyl_carbonyl_carbon: DEPRECATED, ambiguous -- matches any carbonyl bearing an N/O/S neighbour. Retained only so older handoffs still parse. Use phosphate_activated_acyl_carbon.

cofactor_ccd_atoms_notes.alpha_nonbridging_oxygen: Non-bridging oxygen on P-alpha: the charge centre of an in-line substitution at that phosphorus.
cofactor_ccd_atoms_notes.gamma_nonbridging_oxygen: Non-bridging oxygen on P-gamma, likewise for gamma-phosphoryl transfer.

protein_nucleophile_atom.description: Side-chain nucleophile atom of the catalytic residue (Ser OG, Thr OG1, Cys SG). Requires a per-candidate chain/residue/atom assignment; it is NOT derivable from the substrate and must not be guessed.

water_oxygen.description: Oxygen of the hydrolytic water in the deacylation step.

protein_selectors_notes: Protein and solvent roles are resolved from the modelled POSE, not from the substrate SMILES, so a mechanism step referencing them is only executable once the catalytic residue has been assigned for that candidate.
